results.root_cause_actual: PR #881 (api-gateway v9.2.0, deployed 18:40:00Z) raised the PaymentsClient read timeout from 3s to 30s AND simultaneously disabled the payments circuit breaker. When the partner acquirer's p99 latency spiked to 12.4s at 18:47Z, the critical mismatch was between the new 30s gateway read timeout and the unchanged ALB proxy_read_timeout of 10s: the ALB returned a 504 to the client at 10s, but the gateway thread continued holding the upstream connection open for the remaining ~20s. With no circuit breaker to shed further requests, each new payment request consumed a thread for up to 30s. The 64-thread shared pool was exhausted by 18:51:33Z (all 64 threads blocked in PaymentsClient.execute()), causing the accept queue to back up to 611 and denying service to every route — including /v1/orders and /v1/catalog, which do not touch payments-svc — reducing gateway availability to 88.1%.
results.root_cause_expected: PR #881 raised the gateway's payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s (and disabled the circuit breaker) while the edge load balancer's proxy_read_timeout stayed at 10s. When partner latency rose, the edge cut clients off at 10s with 504s while gateway worker threads stayed pinned on the upstream call for the full 30s, saturating the 64-thread pool and taking down routes that never touch payments-svc.

judge.reason: Both identify the same underlying cause: PR #881's change to increase the payments-svc timeout to 30s while disabling the circuit breaker, combined with the edge load balancer's unchanged 10s timeout, causing a timeout mismatch that exhausted the thread pool when partner latency increased.

mechanism: PR #881 deployed at 18:40:00Z raised PAYMENTS_READ_TIMEOUT 3s→30s and disabled PAYMENTS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER in api-gateway v9.2.0
At 18:47Z the partner acquirer p99 latency rose from 1.9s to 12.4s; under v9.1.7 these calls would have failed fast at 3s and been shed by the circuit breaker
With the new 30s timeout and no circuit breaker, each payment request thread in PaymentsClient.execute() now blocked for up to 30s waiting for the slow acquirer
The ALB proxy_read_timeout remained at 10s (unchanged); at 10s the ALB sent a 504 to the client, but the gateway thread continued holding the upstream connection open for the remaining ~20s
As acquirer latency persisted, new payment requests kept arriving, each consuming a thread for ~30s; threads accumulated faster than they were released
By 18:51:33Z all 64/64 worker threads were blocked in PaymentsClient.execute(); the accept queue grew to 611
With the thread pool saturated, no threads were available to serve any route, causing /v1/orders and /v1/catalog (which don't touch payments-svc) to also return 504s
Gateway availability fell to 88.1% across all routes; ALB recorded 4180 504s in a single minute

ruled_out.candidate: Partner acquirer latency spike alone (without the timeout/circuit-breaker change)
ruled_out.why_not: Under v9.1.7 the same acquirer degradation would have caused calls to fail fast at the 3s read timeout and been shed by the circuit breaker, preventing thread accumulation; the deployment record explicitly states 'Under v9.1.7 these calls failed fast at 3s' and there was no incident during v9.1.7's tenure.

ruled_out.candidate: ALB proxy_read_timeout change causing the 504 surge
ruled_out.why_not: The ALB proxy_read_timeout was explicitly unchanged at 10s since 2024 and not touched by PR #881; it is a pre-existing condition, not a change that could have caused the incident to start.

ruled_out.candidate: payments-svc itself being unhealthy or failing
ruled_out.why_not: payments-svc 5xx rate stayed at 0.03% and CPU at 34% both before and after deploy; it was marked healthy and had no deploy since 2026-08-15; no downstream 5xx responses were recorded from it.

ruled_out.candidate: Traffic spike exhausting the thread pool
ruled_out.why_not: No evidence of a traffic volume increase exists; the notable_absences explicitly state 'thread exhaustion appears driven by latency, not volume increase,' and gateway CPU actually dropped from 27% to 8% post-deploy, inconsistent with a traffic spike.

red_herrings.candidate: Partner acquirer latency spike as a standalone cause
red_herrings.why_not: deployment.txt states explicitly: 'Under v9.1.7 these calls failed fast at 3s.' The 3s read timeout and circuit breaker in v9.1.7 would have shed the slow calls before threads accumulated. The acquirer degradation is a necessary co-condition, not the root cause.

red_herrings.candidate: payments-svc being unhealthy or generating 5xx responses
red_herrings.why_not: 2026-08-23T18:56:02.339Z INFO api-gateway payments-svc itself: 5xx rate 0.03%, cpu 34%, healthy — and metrics.json shows payments_svc_5xx_rate_pct unchanged at 0.03% before and after deploy.

red_herrings.candidate: ALB proxy_read_timeout change causing the 504 surge
red_herrings.why_not: deployment.txt and recent_changes.diff both confirm '# NOTE: edge/alb-prod.tf is NOT touched by this PR.' and 'This value has been 10s since 2024 and was not touched by PR #881.' The ALB timeout is a pre-existing condition, not a change.

red_herrings.candidate: Traffic volume spike exhausting the thread pool
red_herrings.why_not: gateway_cpu_pct dropped from 27% to 8% after deploy (metrics.json), inconsistent with increased request volume; threads are blocked on upstream I/O, not executing compute-heavy work.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: payment request lifecycle on the gateway thread vs. the edge timeout seen by the client
cross_file_value_checks.note: The ALB terminates the client connection at 10s, but the gateway thread continues holding the upstream connection for up to 30s. The 20s gap is the window during which threads are stuck with no live client, accumulating until the pool saturates.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: rate at which threads are consumed vs. rate at which they are released
cross_file_value_checks.note: With each thread blocked for up to 30s and acquirer p99 at 12.4s, the pool of 64 threads is exhausted if more than ~5 payment requests arrive per second; the accept queue confirms accumulation to 611 before remediation.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: observed upstream call duration vs. configured ceiling
cross_file_value_checks.note: The observed p99 of 29.9s matches the new 30s timeout ceiling, confirming threads are running right up to the new limit rather than failing fast.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: ability to shed load when the acquirer is slow
cross_file_value_checks.note: Removing the circuit breaker simultaneously with raising the timeout eliminates both fast-fail mechanisms. Either change alone would have left one safety net; removing both together left none.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: thread pool utilisation before and after deploy
cross_file_value_checks.note: Pool went from 14% utilisation to 100%, confirming full saturation post-deploy.
Stable error rate rules out payments-svc as a source of failure; the problem is entirely in the gateway thread pool.

cross_file_value_checks.governs: whether a traffic volume spike caused the thread exhaustion
cross_file_value_checks.note: CPU dropped post-deploy, ruling out a traffic spike as the driver; threads are blocked on I/O wait, not compute.
